question: Do the shove's three Java-bug fixes, router.java_quirks.in_front_of_pad_typo=false (side 0 of ForcedPadRouter.inFrontOfPad takes min(a.x+a.y, b.x+b.y), not b.x+b.x), store_trace_class_self_compare=false (storeTrace compares a contact trace's clearance class with the stored trace's, not with itself) and rational_perp_projection=false (a rational end corner is projected exactly), each alone and together, keep every registered board's routing within N02's totals rule (accept no-regress: correctness fixes) of Java's behaviour, with no new clearance violation; how often does each branch decide a result; and, reported only, does the (c) row in_front_of_pad_side0_flank=false on top of the three change that?
engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (origin/main b93bcd0 plus N06.7's diff), one Linux release build for every arm; profile legacy, so the arms differ from Java only in the four router.java_quirks keys, each given explicitly

baseline.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (origin/main b93bcd0 plus N06.7's diff), one Linux release build for every arm
baseline.what: baseline: all four switches true, Java's shove

in_front_of_pad_typo.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (origin/main b93bcd0 plus N06.7's diff), one Linux release build for every arm

store_trace_class_self_compare.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (origin/main b93bcd0 plus N06.7's diff), one Linux release build for every arm

rational_perp_projection.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (origin/main b93bcd0 plus N06.7's diff), one Linux release build for every arm
rational_perp_projection.what: the exact rational end-corner projection alone

all.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (origin/main b93bcd0 plus N06.7's diff), one Linux release build for every arm
all.what: candidate: the three (b) fixes of batch S together

all_flank.engine: freerouting-rs at the implementing commit (origin/main b93bcd0 plus N06.7's diff), one Linux release build for every arm
all_flank.what: reported: the candidate plus the (c) row in_front_of_pad_side0_flank (side 0's flank takes max)

boards.eligibility: every row; no row is dropped after a number
boards.plugin_row: canary-pwr-plugin: canary-pwr through the KiCad plugin path (plugin_canary below), outside n06_run.py

metric_definitions.unrouted, clearance_violations, vias: the result manifest's board_statistics (connections.incomplete_count, clearance_violations.total_count, vias.total_count): Freerouting's board model on the routed board; n06_run.py copies them into summary.json as `statistics`
metric_definitions.session_differences: 1 if the arm's SES differs byte for byte from the baseline arm's on that board
metric_definitions.shove_*_flips: run_stats counters (--stats json, total.counts): in either arm, the evaluations whose result the switch's other value would flip; in_front_of_pad_typo and in_front_of_pad_side0_flank on side-0 in-front-of-pad tests, store_trace_class_self_compare on end-corner contact tests, rational_perp_projection on rational end-corner entry points
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected, drc_real, via_in_pad,: the canary-pwr plugin row's grade (canary hardware/tools/grade.sh)

accept: Reachability first: if every run's four shove_*_flips counters are 0 and every session equals its baseline, no registered board reaches the branches, and the batch is accepted on its tests (both behaviours pinned).
Sessions identical but a counter above 0: the branch runs but decides nothing that reaches the output; the batch is neutral and accepted.

Otherwise the totals rule for the verdict pair (baseline, all): no new clearance violation on any DSN row, the plugin row's via_in_pad and below_minimum 0 and drc_real no higher than baseline's; the candidate's unrouted summed over the DSN rows plus the plugin row's kicad_unconnected at most the baseline's plus the set's noise, sqrt of the sum of the bands squared (sqrt(5*2^2 + 10^2) = 10.95); no row worse by more than twice its band.
A failed verdict pair is bisected through the three single-switch reported pairs; each switch is judged alone by the same rule.
all_flank (the (c) row) is judged against all by the same rule only if the verdict pair is accepted; otherwise it is reported and in_front_of_pad_side0_flank stays true (N06.12 records the outcome).
stop_rule: One run per arm per row. No heavy run by the implementer.
orchestrator_command: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/orchestrator/n06-target cargo build --release -p freerouting-cli && python3 tools/bench/n06_run.py docs/roadmap/prereg/N06.7.json --out target/orchestrator/n06-s
orchestrator: Run orchestrator_command from the worktree root: it runs each arms.command on each boards.files row (5 rows x 6 arms = 30 runs), checks the input hashes, compares each SES with the baseline's and writes summary.json (session_differences, counts, statistics). It exits non-zero when a session differs, after every run: then apply the totals rule to summary.json's statistics. Then the plugin row.
paired_rule_note: pass_rule is retained for gate parser validation; the registered verdict uses totals with accept=no-regress and the reachability and exact-session guards above.

plugin_canary.source: CANary hardware/canary-pwr-rev1.0, the original KiCad project at canary 9511d9a (git archive, unedited), as in N06.10's plugin-path run; never edit the source project.
plugin_canary.route: For each registered arm, run the release CLI on the plugin-exported DSN with the generated <stem>.args.json args verbatim, then append --router.profile=legacy, the arm's four explicit --router.java_quirks.* flags, --stats json --stats-out <arm>/stats.json and --result-json=<arm>/result.json. One exported input and one argument list serve every arm. Compare each session with the plugin baseline arm's.
plugin_canary.grade: Grade each distinct session's imported copy with canary hardware/tools/grade.sh (ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py); arms with a byte-identical session share one grade. Retain export/import logs, versions, source hashes and grades.

not_registered: time (the fixes change no work budget); the enhanced profile (the arms run under legacy so that only the switches differ from Java)

amendments.reason: main moved on before any N06.7 route (N06.4, N06.5, N06.6, N06.8, N06.12 and Q16.5 were committed after b93bcd0); the registered measurement runs on the tree that would take the promotion. Written before any route of N06.7
amendments.changes: (1) engine base moved from origin/main b93bcd0 with N06.7's diff to main 3b1bde6 (N06.7's diff committed as 1dac842). Every java_quirks switch added since defaults to true (Java), ENHANCED is unchanged, and the arms run under legacy with all four keys explicit, so the arms still differ only in the four keys. The arms' engine, settings and command texts are unchanged; the command's relative binary path target/orchestrator/n06-target/release/freerouting is resolved from the worktree root. (2) Hard-guard check before any number: via_in_pad and below_minimum are the plugin row's only (metric_definitions), and that row runs under legacy (no neck-down) with the canary-graded-flow args. N06.10's graded plugin-path run of the same configuration (legacy, the same exported args, every java_quirks key true) had 0 via-in-pad and 0 below-minimum (KiCad track_width), so the baseline arm does not break a hard guard by construction of the options; the guards are unchanged. (3) How the verdict is computed: freerouting-dev gate --prereg cannot take this registration's records (the DSN rows carry no KiCad grade, so their hard metrics would be null and UNGRADED, and canary-pwr-plugin is not in boards.files, so it would be REFUSED); the accept list is applied by a script to n06_run.py's summary.json (statistics: unrouted, clearance_violations) and the plugin row's grade, exactly as the accept text states, with the registered noise bands. Boards, metrics, arms, the rule and the accept text unchanged
